problems.title: Distance to the xz-plane
problems.question: Find all p so A=(p,4,2) and B=(-1,p²,3) are equally far from the xz-plane.
problems.idea: Distance to the xz-plane is the absolute y-coordinate.
steps: The two distances are 4 and p².
Set p²=4, giving p=2 or p=-2.
problems.note: Both signs are valid; the distance condition cannot select only one.

problems.title: Trapezoid diagonal ratios
problems.question: In the trapezoid with bases AD and BC, diagonals meet at O. Given OC=6 and OD/BO=3/2, find AO.
problems.idea: The two triangles at the parallel bases are similar.

problems.title: Intercept lengths determine the slope magnitude
problems.question: A rising line cuts an x-axis segment twice as long as its y-axis segment. Which is possible: y=2x+1,y=-x+1,y=-x/2+3,y=x/2+1?
problems.idea: For positive slope the two intercepts have opposite signs.
formulas: For y=mx+b, intercept lengths are |b/m| and |b|.
steps: The matching listed function is y=x/2+1.

problems.title: Sum of reciprocal quadratic roots
problems.question: Find 1/r₁+1/r₂ for the roots of 2x²-4x+1=0.
problems.idea: Use Vieta without finding either root.
steps: The product is nonzero, so both reciprocals exist.

problems.title: Intersect two quadratic sign intervals
problems.question: Solve x²-9<0 and x²+2x>0.
problems.idea: Solve each inequality separately.
formulas: x²-9<0 iff -3<x<3; x(x+2)>0 iff x<-2 or x>0.
steps: Keep all endpoints open because both inequalities are strict.

problems.title: Two successive ten-percent price reductions
problems.question: Shoes cost 300 lari on August 3. On the first day of each following month their price falls by 10%. Find their price on October 7 of the same year.
problems.idea: Each reduction multiplies the current price by 0.9.
steps: The first reduction occurs on September 1, giving 300·0.9=270.
The second occurs on October 1, giving 270·0.9=243.
There is no further reduction before October 7.

problems.title: Midpoint distance when a segment crosses a plane
problems.question: The endpoints of a segment are 5 and 3 cm from a plane, and the segment crosses it. Find the midpoint distance.
problems.idea: The endpoints have opposite signed distances.
steps: The midpoint signed distance is (5-3)/2=1, whose absolute value is 1.

problems.title: Determine a parameter in a composition
problems.question: f(x)=2x+1, g(x)=x²-a and f(g(x))=2x²-3. Find a.
problems.idea: Substitute g into f and compare constant terms.

problems.title: A monic parabola tangent to the x-axis
problems.question: The graph y=x²+bx+c touches the x-axis at (4,0). Find c.
problems.idea: Tangency gives a repeated root at x=4.
formulas: y=(x-r)² for a monic quadratic with double root r.

problems.title: Work rate of a more powerful plant
problems.question: One power station produces electricity at three times the rate of the other. How long would the first need to produce what both make in 24 days?
problems.idea: Express all production rates in units of the smaller plant’s rate.
steps: Let the second plant’s daily rate be r. The first has rate 3r, and together they have 4r.

problems.title: Remove absolute values by locating a radical
problems.question: Find |√8-3|+|√8-2|.
problems.idea: Use 2<√8<3 to determine both signs.
steps: √8-3 is negative, so the first term is 3-√8.
√8-2 is positive, so the second is √8-2.
Adding cancels the radicals and gives 1.

problems.title: Disprove a statement with one counterexample
problems.question: Which is false? One statement claims: if -2<x<3, then 4<x²<9.
problems.idea: Squaring an interval that crosses zero does not preserve its lower endpoint.
formulas: A universal claim is false if one permitted input violates its conclusion.
steps: Choose x=0, which lies between -2 and 3.
The other statements follow from subtraction order, the definition of absolute value, and squaring a number less than -3.

problems.title: Square area from its diagonal endpoints
problems.question: A=(2,3),C=(4,9) are opposite vertices of square ABCD. Find its area.
problems.idea: The square area is half its diagonal squared.

problems.title: Scale the input of a quadratic
problems.question: The roots of ax²+bx+c=0 are -3,4. Find the larger root of (a/9)x²+(b/3)x+c=0.
problems.idea: The new polynomial is the original evaluated at x/3.
formulas: P(x/3)=0 iff x/3 is an original root.
steps: The new roots are -9 and 12, so the larger is 12.

problems.title: Bisector length in a 30–60–90 triangle
problems.question: A right triangle’s 60° bisector is 1 cm shorter than its longer leg. Find the bisector length.
problems.idea: Express the sides using the shorter leg s.
formulas: Sides s,√3s,2s; bisector from the angle between b,c has length 2bc cos(A/2)/(b+c).
steps: At the 60° vertex, adjacent sides are s,2s. The bisector is 2(s)(2s)cos30°/(3s)=2√3s/3.
Its difference from the longer leg is √3s-2√3s/3=√3s/3=1, so s=√3.

problems.title: Two adjacent bisectors halve a parallelogram area
problems.question: The bisectors from B,C in parallelogram ABCD meet at M on AD. BM=10,CM=12. Find the parallelogram area.
problems.idea: Adjacent angles are supplementary, so their bisectors are perpendicular.
formulas: B+C=180° ⇒ angle BMC=90°; triangle area=leg product/2.
steps: Triangle BMC is right with area 10·12/2=60.
Its base BC is a full parallelogram side and M lies on opposite side AD, so its altitude equals the parallelogram height.
Its area is half the parallelogram area.

problems.title: Only one integer third side
problems.question: A triangle has sides 5 and 1. Its third side is a positive integer. Find it.
problems.idea: Use strict triangle inequalities.
steps: The only integer in this open interval is 5.

problems.title: Median versus bisector at a right angle
problems.question: A right triangle has an acute angle 15°. Find the angle between the median and angle bisector from the right vertex.
problems.idea: The median points toward the midpoint of the hypotenuse.
formulas: Right-angle bisector makes 45° with either leg; the median direction has the same slope as the opposite hypotenuse endpoint ratio.
steps: Put the right vertex at the origin and the other vertices at (a,0),(0,b). The midpoint is (a/2,b/2).
The median makes angle arctan(b/a), which is 15° or 75° depending on leg labels.
Its angle with the 45° bisector is 30° in either case.

problems.title: Choose the geometric ratio using the first-term sign
problems.question: A geometric progression has negative first term, b₅-b₁=15 and b₄-b₂=6. Find its ratio r.
problems.idea: Divide to eliminate the first term, then test its sign.
steps: The nonzero differences allow division, giving (r²+1)/r=15/6=5/2.
Because b₁<0 while b₁(r⁴-1)=15>0, we need |r|<1.

problems.title: Percentage change of a fraction
problems.question: A positive fraction’s numerator decreases 50% and denominator increases 25%. Find the percentage decrease in its value.
problems.idea: Divide the two scaling factors.

problems.title: A head start and an eventual separation
problems.question: Two cars travel in the same direction at 60 and 75 km/h. The slower starts 2 hours earlier. How long after the faster starts are they 180 km apart?
problems.idea: The signed separation changes at the relative speed.
steps: Solve |120-15t|=180. The two algebraic times are -4 and 20 hours.
Only t≥0 is relevant, so the answer is 20 hours, after the faster car passes the slower.

problems.title: A product of consecutive integers is even
problems.question: For consecutive integers a,b,c, which is always odd: a+b+c,abc,a+b+c+1,abc-1?
problems.idea: At least one factor in the product is even.
steps: The product abc is always even.
Therefore abc-1 is always odd. The parity of the two sums varies with the middle integer.

problems.title: Last age in an arithmetic progression
problems.question: Six people enter in age order, each 2 years older than the previous one. Their mean age is 30. Find the last age.
problems.idea: The mean equals the average of the first and last terms.
steps: If the first age is a, the mean is a+5=30, so a=25.

problems.title: A nonpositive sum of absolute values
problems.question: Solve |x²-4x+3|+|x²+3x-4|≤0.
problems.idea: Each term is nonnegative, so both must vanish.
steps: The first polynomial factors as (x-1)(x-3), with zeros 1,3.
The second factors as (x-1)(x+4), with zeros 1,-4.

problems.title: Middle term times the number of terms
problems.question: An arithmetic progression has a₉=20. Find S₁₇.
problems.idea: There are eight symmetric pairs around the ninth term.
formulas: For an odd number of arithmetic terms, sum=number·middle term.

problems.title: Minimum sequence term at an integer vertex
problems.question: Find the smallest term of xₙ=n²-6n+7, n=1,2,….
problems.idea: Complete the square.
steps: The squared term is nonnegative and is zero at the allowed index n=3.

problems.title: Hypotenuse segments inherit squared leg ratios
problems.question: A right triangle has leg ratio 3:2. The altitude divides its hypotenuse into two parts differing by 2 m. Find the hypotenuse.
problems.idea: Their ratio is 9:4.
steps: Write the two pieces as 9t,4t. Their difference 5t=2 gives t=2/5.

problems.title: Recover the missing second equation from the Word source
problems.question: Solve |x|=5, x+y=7.
problems.idea: The PDF lost the second equation, but it survives in the embedded Word equation.
problems.note: The original Word file 098_2015_16_g12.docx, embedded equation image15.wmf, preserves x+y=7 even though the PDF renders it incorrectly.

problems.title: Perimeter of a right tangential trapezoid
problems.question: A right trapezoid has inradius 4 cm and obtuse angle 150°. Find its perimeter.
problems.idea: The height is the circle diameter, and the other acute angle is 30°.
formulas: h=2r; sloping leg=h/sin30°; in a tangential quadrilateral, opposite-side sums agree.
steps: h=8 and the sloping leg is 16. The perpendicular leg is 8.
Thus the perimeter is twice 24, namely 48.

problems.title: A rational inequality with a forbidden pole
problems.question: Solve 2/(x-3)>1.
problems.idea: Move everything to one side and test signs.
steps: The quotient is positive only between them. The pole and zero are excluded.

problems.title: Substitute a linear equation into a quadratic system
problems.question: Solve 4x²+1=y²+4x, y-x=3.
problems.idea: Replace y with x+3.
steps: Use y=x+3 to get y=7/3 or 7.

problems.title: A parameter giving a positive linear root
problems.question: For which t does 3(2-x)=4(t-2x) have a positive root?
problems.idea: Solve for x first.
steps: Since the denominator 5 is positive, x>0 iff 4t-6>0.
problems.note: A single choice t=2 is an example, and (1.5,5) is a subset of valid values, but the full parameter set is (1.5,∞).

problems.title: Incircle radius from trapezoid bases
problems.question: An isosceles trapezoid circumscribes a circle and has bases 2,8. Find the circle radius.
problems.idea: Tangency determines the equal legs.
steps: The circle radius is half this height: 2.

problems.title: Bus speeds from the fraction of route completed
problems.question: Two buses start together. When the faster arrives, the slower has 1/5 of the route left. The faster is 20 km/h quicker. Find its speed.
problems.idea: Equal travel times make distance and speed ratios equal.
steps: The faster speed is 100 km/h, and the slower is 80.

problems.title: Trapezoid area from two opposite triangles
problems.question: In a trapezoid with bases AD and BC, diagonal-intersection triangles AOD,BOC have areas 36,16. Find its area.
problems.idea: The square roots of these areas add before squaring.
formulas: S=(√S₁+√S₂)² for triangles on the two parallel bases.
steps: The two side triangles each have area √(36·16)=24.
problems.note: This uses AD and BC as the bases, consistent with the unequal given triangle areas. If AB and CD were the bases, AOD and BOC would have equal areas, contradicting 36 and 16.

problems.title: A line and parabola share two points
problems.question: y=kx and y=-x²+bx+c meet at (0,0),(-4,-12). Find k,b,c.
problems.idea: Substitute both shared points.
formulas: A point on a graph satisfies its equation.
steps: The origin gives c=0. The line through (-4,-12) gives k=3.

problems.title: The sine rule with exact angles
problems.question: In triangle ABC, A=30°,B=105°,AC=10 cm. Find AB,BC.
problems.idea: The third angle is 45°.

problems.title: A perpendicular segment inside a square
problems.question: Square ABCD has side 4. E∈AB,F∈BC, ∠EFD=90°,FD=5. Find EF.
problems.idea: Coordinates turn the length and right angle into equations.
formulas: Distance formula; perpendicular vectors have zero dot product.
steps: Take A=(0,0),B=(4,0),C=(4,4),D=(0,4),E=(e,0),F=(4,f). FD²=16+(f-4)²=25 gives f=1; f=7 is outside the side.
FE=(e-4,-1),FD=(-4,3). Their dot product is -4(e-4)-3=0, giving e=13/4.

problems.title: Recover the route length from time saved
problems.question: A bus normally averages 40 km/h. It finishes the first half 20 minutes late, then travels the second half at 45 km/h to arrive on time. Find the route length.
problems.idea: The second half must recover exactly 1/3 hour.

problems.title: Incentre distance is a side-weighted average
problems.question: Triangle ABC is entirely on one side of a plane. Its vertex distances are 13,10,15 cm, and AB=6,BC=9,AC=10. Find the incentre distance.
problems.idea: The incentre’s barycentric weights are the opposite side lengths.
steps: The opposite side weights for A,B,C are a=9,b=10,c=6.
All signed distances have the same sign, so ordinary distance can be averaged directly.
